Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

anxious adjective

also worried, uneasy, nervous, nervousness, tense

classical

Cic. Tusc. 4.27; Cic. Fin. 2.55: ānxiō animō aut sollicitō esse (Lewis & Short)
Andresian p. 36
Traupman 272

ānxius, ānxia, ānxium

anxious, uneasy, troubled

Cicero’s word for anxiety as a lasting cast of mind, against angī, to be in distress for a moment (Tusc. 4.27). The vowel is long before -nx-, which Lewis & Short leaves unmarked.

Other words

  • sollicitus, sollicita, sollicitum — worried, uneasy

    also used · classical · Cic. Fin. 2.55 (Lewis & Short, s.v. ānxius)

    The everyday word for being worried about something: sollicitus sum dē tē.

  • trepidus, trepida, trepidum — alarmed, nervous

    also used · classical · Traupman 156

  • trepidātiō, trepidātiōnis f. — alarm, agitation, nervousness

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Traupman 156

  • intentus, intenta, intentum — strained, tense

    also used · classical · Traupman 156, 158

    Properly “stretched, intent”; Traupman’s word for nervous and tense.

See also concern.
